$schema_note: Shot list v1.2 — see shot_list_01_act_one.json for field conventions. Beat-level location/look/wear are defaults; VO and dialogue are referenced from the locked screenplay.
status: draft — v2.0 drama rewrite shot list update
rules: Restrained violence: death is shown through absence — an empty pit, a dropped object, a rifle with no owner. No wounds, no bodies. Silence-first: the cue from Act Three fades in 4.1; the burial is silent.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-03
dialogue_refs.delivery: Mostafa spits sand from his mouth and shouts toward Sayed without moving from the wall. The question escapes him before he can make himself sound brave.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-02
dialogue_refs.delivery: Sayed answers Mostafa while still shielding the optic. Punch the first sentence across the noise, then give the second a dry, weighty certainty rather than playing it as a speech.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-06
dialogue_refs.delivery: He watches the impact, then sees the empty launcher. Let a tiny breath of laughter escape before the words; he is speaking mainly to himself, not celebrating.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-03
dialogue_refs.delivery: Catch Sayed at arm’s length just before he climbs out. Keep a full young man’s chest voice; the plea escapes despite Mostafa’s effort to sound ready for the same danger.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-02
dialogue_refs.emotion: protective resolve concealed as an order
dialogue_refs.delivery: Answer while tapping the letter in Mostafa’s pocket, using the task to keep him behind. Do not play a farewell or ask for sympathy; make the finality plain and practical.

shots.prompt: the young private sitting at the bottom of his pit, back against the sand wall, knees drawn up

shots.prompt: the young private buttoning the letter back into his pocket, picking up his rifle, rising to look over the lip of the pit

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-01
dialogue_refs.delivery: Keep his eyes on the line rather than on Mahmoud. Leave a slight weight before «يَا مَحْمُودْ»; he is forcing himself to turn loss into an order.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-04
dialogue_refs.delivery: Let the look absorb the meaning before he answers. The words stay automatic and disciplined; no tremble or added emphasis.

beats.title: Blackout

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-14
dialogue_refs.delivery: An 8-year-old in the dark, wide awake under the blanket, asking quietly.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-13
dialogue_refs.delivery: She does not answer the question; soft, the voice steady only by effort.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-14
dialogue_refs.delivery: He notices that she is still sitting up and quietly catches her in the evasion. Let the question rise naturally, without sounding accusatory.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-13
dialogue_refs.delivery: Answer with a tired smile he cannot see, keeping the first word reassuring. After the pause, place a soft emphasis on «إِنْتَ» as she makes his sleep—not her fear—the subject.

shots.prompt: hands smoothing sand over a grave in moonlight

shots.notes: v2 restage: no spoken prayer; Shalabi kneels at the last grave smoothing the sand. v2 drama rewrite (2026-10-15): speaker on camera, lip-synced.

shots.prompt: night in the flat desert: the radio operator standing motionless with the silent backpack radio and its whip antenna on his back, facing the camera, his face lit by the warm orange glow of distant burning tanks on the horizon behind the camera, the fire reflected in his taped wire-rimmed glasses, the background dark blue, his face clearly readable

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-01
dialogue_refs.delivery: Speak down toward the grave, not out to the men. Let the pause carry the loss; the second phrase should come on a failing breath, without sobbing or declamation.
